scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Panyembrama was designed in response to late 1960s controversies over performing sacred Balinese dances for secular non-Balinese audiences and tourists.
Choreographer I Wayan Beratha of the Karawitan Conservatory was commissioned to create a secular alternative.
He combined elements of traditional legong, condong, and pendet dances.
on_screen: Map: Indonesia · Southeast Asia
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Derived from the Balinese word 'sambrama' meaning 'welcome', Panyembrama serves as an opening welcoming dance at events, often preceding a secular legong.
Although created as a secular dance for tourists, it is also taught in dance academies and performed at temples as a welcome for deities.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed by groups of two or more young women.
Dancers begin kneeling as if praying, then perform slow welcoming gestures accompanied by gamelan music.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Dancers wear layered clothing decorated with golden prada patterns, including a kamben (sarong) and a chest-to-waist wrap.
Heads are adorned with golden headdresses and frangipani flowers.
Dancers carry silver or aluminium metal dishes containing incense and flower petals.

scenes.title: The people
narration: I Wayan Beratha created and choreographed the dance for the Karawitan Conservatory.
Art critic A. M. Hermin Kusmayati classified it as a form of classical dance, and ethnomusicologist Zachar Laskewicz analyzed its textual connections to traditional dance.
Panyembrama incorporates movements from legong, condong, and pendet.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Panyembrama is influence of Legong: Panyembrama incorporates movements from legong and is frequently performed immediately before secularized legong.
Panyembrama is influence of Pendet: Panyembrama adapted traditional greeting and flower-scattering elements from pendet.
Panyembrama is influence of Condong: Panyembrama integrated stylistic movement elements from condong.
Panyembrama is sibling of Oleg Tamulilingan: Created during the same era to provide non-sacred Balinese dance repertoire for non-Balinese audiences.
